subject: game_design

resources.title: Game Design
resources.notes: Practical design and analysis of games through team projects, rules design, iteration and extensive playtesting.

resources.title: Game Design
resources.notes: Historical and analytical game-design course with original game projects, documented testing, mechanics analysis and iteration.

resources.title: Learn to Build Your Own Videogame with the Unity Game Engine and Microsoft Kinect
resources.notes: No prior programming or game-design experience required; guided and team projects cover videogame creation, Unity, GitHub collaboration, 3D objects, gesture input and team management.

resources.title: Creating Video Games
resources.notes: Multidisciplinary teams design, develop, test and focus-test original digital games; emphasizes iteration across design, audio, aesthetics, fiction, programming and production.

resources.title: Introduction to Videogame Studies
resources.notes: Interdisciplinary study and analysis of videogames; no programming prerequisite, with additional work for graduate students.

resources.title: Computer Games and Simulations for Education and Exploration
resources.notes: Students design games and examine learning outcomes, research/development issues and field testing.

resources.title: Game Design and Game Technology Research Discovery
resources.notes: Research discovery only; individual papers require provenance, evidence-quality, version and license verification before use.

resources.title: CS 188 Pacman Projects
resources.notes: Structured Pacman projects apply search, multi-agent reasoning, reinforcement learning and probabilistic inference. Beginner mapping denotes the first scaffolded project sequence, not beginner-level computer science overall.

resources.title: Computer Game Programming
resources.notes: Advanced implementation course covering real-time game systems and production-oriented programming; it is not mapped to foundation or beginner levels.

resources.title: Unity ML-Agents Toolkit Documentation
resources.notes: Official documentation for training intelligent agents in Unity environments. Mapping reflects implementation practice; documentation alone does not establish research mastery.

resources.title: Game Accessibility Guidelines
resources.notes: Practical guidance organized by basic, intermediate and advanced implementation effort. It strengthens applied accessibility coverage but is not treated as a graduate curriculum or research corpus.

resources.title: Foundations of Digital Games Proceedings
resources.notes: Peer-reviewed research venue spanning game design, technical systems, AI, production and player experience. Proceedings support research discovery; each paper must still pass item-level evidence and rights checks.

known_gaps: Foundation-level game mechanics, systems design and game AI still need dedicated no-prerequisite curricula before full catalog coverage can be claimed.
Beginner systems-design coverage remains thinner than core design, programming and production coverage.
Research proceedings and repositories are evidence-discovery layers; they do not by themselves establish learner mastery or runtime retrieval quality.
notes: Mappings use only the existing game_design taxonomy keys.
Level assignments are resource-specific and intentionally conservative.
Catalog coverage does not prove ATLAS can ingest, retrieve, cite or apply the material.
